items.prompt:
Group behavior can help animals
A) survive and reproduce
B) never survive
C) only sleep
D) stop eating

steps: Groups can improve survival and reproduction.

items.prompt:
Meerkats taking turns on guard help the group by
A) warning of predators
B) eating all the food
C) attracting predators
D) doing nothing

steps: Guards warn the group of danger.

items.prompt:
Wolves hunt in packs so they can
A) catch large prey for more food
B) sleep more
C) swim faster
D) fly
items.answer: A) catch large prey for more food

steps: Packs catch prey a lone wolf cannot.

items.prompt:
Evidence that group behavior helps survival would compare
A) grouped animals with solitary animals
B) rocks with water
C) colors of fur
D) the weather
items.answer: A) grouped animals with solitary animals

steps: Comparing grouped and solitary outcomes is evidence.

items.prompt:
Bees in a hive help each other by
A) sharing work like gathering food and caring for young
B) working alone
C) ignoring the hive
D) leaving the young
items.answer: A) sharing work like gathering food and caring for young

steps: Shared work lets the hive thrive.

items.prompt:
Which is a COST of living in a group?
A) Competition for food within the group
B) Better defense
C) More food found
D) Shared care of young
items.answer: A) Competition for food within the group

steps: Groups can compete and spread disease, a cost.

items.prompt:
Evaluate: 'Group living has only benefits and no costs.' This is
A) incomplete, because groups also have costs like competition and disease spread
B) completely true
C) proof groups are bad
D) about plants only
items.answer: A) incomplete, because groups also have costs like competition and disease spread

steps: Groups have both benefits and costs.

items.prompt:
Group behavior helps a species most when
A) the benefits outweigh the costs
B) there are no benefits
C) the costs are largest
D) animals live alone
items.answer: A) the benefits outweigh the costs

steps: Net benefit determines whether grouping helps.
